fieldlist.field: Four days on foot from Takijiri to Nachi, through the cedars of the Kii peninsula. Twenty-seven photos, in the order they were taken.
At twenty to four we were at the river in Takijiri, a quarter of an hour later on the trail. The first hour does not pretend: steps, roots, then more steps.

The morning began above the clouds and ended at a gate of paper lanterns. In between, stone paving that stays grippy when wet, a stream under the cedars and a bright orange crab that did not move for the camera.

The bird in the logo is the Yatagarasu, messenger of the Kumano deities. According to the old chronicles it guided Emperor Jimmu through the mountains from Kumano to Yamato. Its three legs are often read as heaven, earth and humankind. On the trail you meet it on shrine banners and on the goōhōin talismans, and on the middle lantern of the gate in Chikatsuyu.
The longest day. From Chikatsuyu through the cedars and past a small oji shrine to Hongu, then on to Yunomine. By four we were sitting in a stone pool under a wooden roof.
Over the Kogumotori-goe and the Ogumotori-goe to Nachi, where the pagoda stands in front of the falls. In Katsuura a ferry took us across the harbour to a ryokan with a view of the water.
Two days later, the last evening. The light came out for twenty minutes. April 25, 17:37
The order of the stations and the day boundaries are right, the geometry is not. For navigation you need the tourism office map.
Schematic map of the route with six stations
Two emails a year, whenever a new route is written up
Next time the Kohechi, the mountain path from Koyasan to Hongu. No marketing, no sharing of your address.

ロゴの鳥は八咫烏、熊野の神々の使いです。古い記録によれば、神武天皇を熊野から大和へと山中で導いたとされます。三本の足は天・地・人を表すとよく言われます。道中では神社の幟や熊野牛王宝印の護符に、そして近露の門の真ん中の提灯にも姿を見せます。

近露 → 本宮 → 湯の峰
いちばん長い日。近露から杉林を抜け、小さな王子の社を過ぎて本宮へ、さらに湯の峰へ。4時には木の屋根の下の石の湯船に浸かっていた。

Der Morgen begann über den Wolken und endete an einem Tor aus Papierlaternen. Dazwischen Steinpflaster, das auch nass griffig bleibt, ein Bach unter den Zedern und eine leuchtend orange Krabbe, die für die Kamera stillhielt.

Der Vogel im Logo ist die Yatagarasu, Botin der Kumano-Gottheiten. Den alten Chroniken nach führte sie Kaiser Jimmu durch die Berge von Kumano nach Yamato. Ihre drei Beine werden oft als Himmel, Erde und Mensch gedeutet. Am Weg begegnet man ihr auf Schreinfahnen, den Goōhōin-Amuletten und auf der mittleren Laterne des Tors in Chikatsuyu.

Do I need to book accommodation in advance?
Yes, and early. Takahara and Chikatsuyu each have a handful of minshuku, and in spring and autumn they are full months ahead. The Tanabe tourism office reservation service books in English.

The Tanabe tourism office reservation service books in English.","title":"Do I need to book accommodation in advance?","value":"","variant":"default","x":"0","y":"0"}
Muss ich die Unterkünfte im Voraus buchen?
Ja, und früh. Takahara und Chikatsuyu haben je eine Handvoll Minshuku, und im Frühling und Herbst sind sie Monate vorher voll. Der Reservierungsdienst des Tourismusbüros in Tanabe bucht auf Englisch.

{"active":"0","anchor":"middle","badge":"","boundary":"0","direction":"forward","fieldname":"tx_kumanokodo_items","hidden":"0","icon":"clock","image":"0","l10n_source":"0","label":"","label_y":"0","link":"","link_label":"","meta":"","note":"","open":"1","shift":"0","span":"6","subtitle":"","text":"Yes, and early. Takahara and Chikatsuyu each have a handful of minshuku, and in spring and autumn they are full months ahead. The Tanabe tourism office reservation service books in English.","title":"Do I need to book accommodation in advance?","value":"","variant":"default","x":"0","y":"0"}
宿は事前に予約が必要ですか？
はい、早めに。高原と近露には民宿が数軒ずつしかなく、春と秋は数か月前に満室になります。田辺市観光協会の予約サービスは英語でも対応しています。

{"active":"0","anchor":"middle","badge":"","boundary":"0","direction":"forward","fieldname":"tx_kumanokodo_items","hidden":"0","icon":"clock","image":"0","l10n_source":"0","label":"","label_y":"0","link":"","link_label":"","meta":"","note":"","open":"0","shift":"0","span":"6","subtitle":"","text":"The Kii peninsula is one of the wettest regions of Japan. Waterproof boots and gaiters help less than you hope; a dry change of clothes in a sealed bag helps more.","title":"How much rain should I expect?","value":"","variant":"default","x":"0","y":"0"}
雨はどのくらい降りますか？
紀伊半島は日本でも特に雨の多い地域です。防水の靴やスパッツは思ったほど役に立たず、密封袋に入れた乾いた着替えのほうが助かります。

Buses link the villages along the route several times a day, which makes it easy to shorten a day or to get back to the start.","title":"Can you get around by bus?","value":"","variant":"default","x":"0","y":"0"}
バスで移動できますか？
はい。ルート沿いの集落を一日に何本かバスが結んでいるので、一日を短くしたり出発地へ戻ったりしやすいです。

{"active":"0","anchor":"middle","badge":"","boundary":"0","direction":"forward","fieldname":"tx_kumanokodo_items","hidden":"0","icon":"clock","image":"0","l10n_source":"0","label":"","label_y":"0","link":"","link_label":"","meta":"","note":"","open":"0","shift":"0","span":"6","subtitle":"","text":"Yes, between the main villages, booked through the Tanabe tourism office one day ahead.","title":"Is there a luggage transfer?","value":"","variant":"default","x":"0","y":"0"}
荷物の配送はありますか？
はい、主な集落の間で利用でき、前日までに田辺市観光協会で予約します。

Waterproof boots and gaiters help less than you hope; a dry change of clothes in a sealed bag helps more.","title":"How much rain should I expect?","value":"","variant":"default","x":"0","y":"0"}
Mit wie viel Regen muss man rechnen?
Die Kii-Halbinsel gehört zu den regenreichsten Gegenden Japans. Wasserdichte Schuhe und Gamaschen helfen weniger als erhofft; trockene Wechselkleidung in einem dichten Beutel hilft mehr.

Buses link the villages along the route several times a day, which makes it easy to shorten a day or to get back to the start.","title":"Can you get around by bus?","value":"","variant":"default","x":"0","y":"0"}
Kommt man mit dem Bus voran?
Ja. Busse verbinden die Orte entlang der Route mehrmals am Tag. So lässt sich ein Tag verkürzen oder man kommt zum Start zurück.

Ja, zwischen den größeren Orten, einen Tag vorher über das Tourismusbüro in Tanabe gebucht.
How much rain should I expect?
The Kii peninsula is one of the wettest regions of Japan. Waterproof boots and gaiters help less than you hope; a dry change of clothes in a sealed bag helps more.
Can you get around by bus?
Yes. Buses link the villages along the route several times a day, which makes it easy to shorten a day or to get back to the start.
Yes, between the main villages, booked through the Tanabe tourism office one day ahead.

Uhrzeiten aus den Fotos, nicht aus einem Plan.
Times from the photos, not from a plan.

Between Takijiri and Hongu the trail crosses passes barely higher than 700 metres, and still it feels remote. The forests are planted sugi cedars, set close together; when the mist settles between them you cannot see twenty metres ahead.

Along the way you pass the oji, small roadside shrines where pilgrims once stopped to pray. Most are a clearing, a stone and a wooden torii, easy to walk past if you are looking at your feet.

Zwischen Takijiri und Hongu quert der Weg Pässe, die kaum höher als 700 Meter sind, und trotzdem wirkt er abgelegen. Die Wälder sind gepflanzte Sugi-Zedern, dicht an dicht; wenn sich Nebel zwischen sie legt, sieht man keine zwanzig Meter weit.

Unterwegs kommt man an den Oji vorbei, kleinen Schreinen am Weg, an denen Pilger früher beteten. Meist sind es eine Lichtung, ein Stein und ein hölzernes Torii, leicht zu übersehen, wenn man auf die Füße schaut.

滝尻から本宮まで、道は標高700メートルにも満たない峠を越えていくのに、どこか人里離れた感じがする。森は植林された杉が密に並び、霧が立ち込めると二十メートル先も見えない。

道中では王子を通り過ぎる。かつて参詣者が祈った道端の小さな社だ。たいていは空き地と石と木の鳥居だけで、足元ばかり見ていると見落としてしまう。
The Kumano Kodo is not one long trail but a network of old pilgrim paths to three shrines. We walked the Nakahechi in April, from Takijiri to Nachi, in four days.
Four days through the cedar mist
A path in use for a thousand years

The bird in the logo is the Yatagarasu, messenger of the Kumano deities. According to the old chronicles it guided Emperor Jimmu through the mountains from Kumano to Yamato. Its three legs are often read as heaven, earth and humankind. On the trail you meet it on shrine banners and on the goōhōin talismans, and on the middle lantern of the gate in Chikatsuyu.
“Dinner is at six. The bath is open until eleven.”
The order of the stations and the day boundaries are right, the geometry is not. For navigation you need the tourism office map.
Schematic map of the route with six stations
The four that came up most often.
Two emails a year, whenever a new route is written up
Next time the Kohechi, the mountain path from Koyasan to Hongu. No marketing, no sharing of your address.

ロゴの鳥は八咫烏、熊野の神々の使いです。古い記録によれば、神武天皇を熊野から大和へと山中で導いたとされます。三本の足は天・地・人を表すとよく言われます。道中では神社の幟や熊野牛王宝印の護符に、そして近露の門の真ん中の提灯にも姿を見せます。

Der Vogel im Logo ist die Yatagarasu, Botin der Kumano-Gottheiten. Den alten Chroniken nach führte sie Kaiser Jimmu durch die Berge von Kumano nach Yamato. Ihre drei Beine werden oft als Himmel, Erde und Mensch gedeutet. Am Weg begegnet man ihr auf Schreinfahnen, den Goōhōin-Amuletten und auf der mittleren Laterne des Tors in Chikatsuyu.

Beim nächsten Mal der Kohechi, der Bergpfad von Koyasan nach Hongu. Keine Werbung, keine Weitergabe Ihrer Adresse.
Do I need to book accommodation in advance?
Yes, and early. Takahara and Chikatsuyu each have a handful of minshuku, and in spring and autumn they are full months ahead. The Tanabe tourism office reservation service books in English.

Muss ich die Unterkünfte im Voraus buchen?
Ja, und früh. Takahara und Chikatsuyu haben je eine Handvoll Minshuku, und im Frühling und Herbst sind sie Monate vorher voll. Der Reservierungsdienst des Tourismusbüros in Tanabe bucht auf Englisch.

宿は事前に予約が必要ですか？
はい、早めに。高原と近露には民宿が数軒ずつしかなく、春と秋は数か月前に満室になります。田辺市観光協会の予約サービスは英語でも対応しています。

Waterproof boots and gaiters help less than you hope; a dry change of clothes in a sealed bag helps more.","title":"How much rain should I expect?","value":"","variant":"default","x":"0","y":"0"}
雨はどのくらい降りますか？
紀伊半島は日本でも特に雨の多い地域です。防水の靴やスパッツは思ったほど役に立たず、密封袋に入れた乾いた着替えのほうが助かります。

バスで移動できますか？
はい。ルート沿いの集落を一日に何本かバスが結んでいるので、一日を短くしたり出発地へ戻ったりしやすいです。

荷物の配送はありますか？
はい、主な集落の間で利用でき、前日までに田辺市観光協会で予約します。

Waterproof boots and gaiters help less than you hope; a dry change of clothes in a sealed bag helps more.","title":"How much rain should I expect?","value":"","variant":"default","x":"0","y":"0"}
Mit wie viel Regen muss man rechnen?
Die Kii-Halbinsel gehört zu den regenreichsten Gegenden Japans. Wasserdichte Schuhe und Gamaschen helfen weniger als erhofft; trockene Wechselkleidung in einem dichten Beutel hilft mehr.

Ja. Busse verbinden die Orte entlang der Route mehrmals am Tag. So lässt sich ein Tag verkürzen oder man kommt zum Start zurück.

How much rain should I expect?
The Kii peninsula is one of the wettest regions of Japan. Waterproof boots and gaiters help less than you hope; a dry change of clothes in a sealed bag helps more.
Can you get around by bus?
Yes. Buses link the villages along the route several times a day, which makes it easy to shorten a day or to get back to the start.
Yes, between the main villages, booked through the Tanabe tourism office one day ahead.

Clouds lying in the valley at seven. Stone paving, a stream, a land crab at noon, the lantern gate of Chikatsuyu at 17:28.
The longest day, about 25 kilometres through the cedars to Hongu, and on to Yunomine. At four an outdoor bath.
Over the Kogumotori-goe and the Ogumotori-goe to Nachi and the pagoda in front of the falls. In Katsuura a ferry to the ryokan.

Beim nächsten Mal der Kohechi, der Bergpfad von Koyasan nach Hongu. Keine Werbung, keine Weitergabe Ihrer Adresse.
All twenty-seven photos, day by day, in the order they were taken.
At twenty to four we were at the river in Takijiri, a quarter of an hour later on the trail. The first hour does not pretend: steps, roots, then more steps.

The morning began above the clouds and ended at a gate of paper lanterns. In between, stone paving that stays grippy when wet, a stream under the cedars and a bright orange crab that did not move for the camera.
The longest day. From Chikatsuyu through the cedars and past a small oji shrine to Hongu, then on to Yunomine. By four we were sitting in a stone pool under a wooden roof.
Over the Kogumotori-goe and the Ogumotori-goe to Nachi, where the pagoda stands in front of the falls. In Katsuura a ferry took us across the harbour to a ryokan with a view of the water.
Two days later, the last evening. The light came out for twenty minutes. April 25, 17:37

近露 → 本宮 → 湯の峰
いちばん長い日。近露から杉林を抜け、小さな王子の社を過ぎて本宮へ、さらに湯の峰へ。4時には木の屋根の下の石の湯船に浸かっていた。

Was wir allen sagen würden, die den Nakahechi planen: Anreise, Unterkunft, Wegmarkierung und welche Karten man mitnehmen sollte.
Was man uns danach gefragt hat
Do I need to book accommodation in advance?
Yes, and early. Takahara and Chikatsuyu each have a handful of minshuku, and in spring and autumn they are full months ahead. The Tanabe tourism office reservation service books in English.

Muss ich die Unterkünfte im Voraus buchen?
Ja, und früh. Takahara und Chikatsuyu haben je eine Handvoll Minshuku, und im Frühling und Herbst sind sie Monate vorher voll. Der Reservierungsdienst des Tourismusbüros in Tanabe bucht auf Englisch.

宿は事前に予約が必要ですか？
はい、早めに。高原と近露には民宿が数軒ずつしかなく、春と秋は数か月前に満室になります。田辺市観光協会の予約サービスは英語でも対応しています。

雨はどのくらい降りますか？
紀伊半島は日本でも特に雨の多い地域です。防水の靴やスパッツは思ったほど役に立たず、密封袋に入れた乾いた着替えのほうが助かります。

バスで移動できますか？
はい。ルート沿いの集落を一日に何本かバスが結んでいるので、一日を短くしたり出発地へ戻ったりしやすいです。

荷物の配送はありますか？
はい、主な集落の間で利用でき、前日までに田辺市観光協会で予約します。

Mit wie viel Regen muss man rechnen?
Die Kii-Halbinsel gehört zu den regenreichsten Gegenden Japans. Wasserdichte Schuhe und Gamaschen helfen weniger als erhofft; trockene Wechselkleidung in einem dichten Beutel hilft mehr.

Ja. Busse verbinden die Orte entlang der Route mehrmals am Tag. So lässt sich ein Tag verkürzen oder man kommt zum Start zurück.

中辺路には数百メートルごとに番号付きの木の道標が立っている。自分の位置を誰かに伝えるときに番号が役に立つ。

一日分の水と食べ物を持っていくこと。集落の間では何も買えない。

大雨のあとは道の一部が通行止めになることがある。出発前に観光協会のお知らせを確認すること。

Along the Nakahechi you sleep in minshuku, small family guest houses. Dinner and breakfast are usually included, and dinner is early.

Takahara and Chikatsuyu have only a handful of them. In spring and autumn they are full months ahead, so book the whole walk at once.

The Tanabe tourism office runs a reservation service in English that books the whole route.

Am Nakahechi schläft man in Minshuku, kleinen Familienpensionen. Abendessen und Frühstück sind meist dabei, und das Abendessen ist früh.

Takahara und Chikatsuyu haben nur eine Handvoll davon. Im Frühling und Herbst sind sie Monate vorher voll, also am besten die ganze Wanderung auf einmal buchen.

Das Tourismusbüro in Tanabe betreibt einen Reservierungsdienst auf Englisch, der die ganze Route bucht.

Along the Nakahechi you sleep in minshuku, small family guest houses. Dinner and breakfast are usually included, and dinner is early.<\/p>\r\n

Takahara and Chikatsuyu have only a handful of them. In spring and autumn they are full months ahead, so book the whole walk at once.<\/p>\r\n

The Tanabe tourism office runs a reservation service in English that books the whole route.<\/p>","bullets_type":"0","categories":"0","category_field":"","colPos":"0","cols":"0","date":"0","editlock":"0","endtime":"0","fe_group":"0","file_collections":"","filelink_size":"0","filelink_sorting":"","filelink_sorting_direction":"","frame_class":"default","header":"","header_layout":"0","header_link":"","header_position":"","hidden":"0","image":"0","image_zoom":"0","imageborder":"0","imagecols":"2","imageheight":"","imageorient":"0","imagewidth":"","l10n_source":"0","layout":"0","linkToTop":"0","media":"0","pages":"","pi_flexform":"","records":"","recursive":"0","rowDescription":"","sectionIndex":"1","selected_categories":"","space_after_class":"","space_before_class":"","starttime":"0","subheader":"","table_caption":"","table_class":"","table_delimiter":"124","table_enclosure":"0","table_header_position":"0","table_tfoot":"0","target":"","tx_impexp_origuid":"0","tx_kumanokodo_align":"start","tx_kumanokodo_anchor":"","tx_kumanokodo_aside":"","tx_kumanokodo_bleed":"0","tx_kumanokodo_column":"a","tx_kumanokodo_column_a":"0","tx_kumanokodo_column_b":"0","tx_kumanokodo_column_gap":"40","tx_kumanokodo_columns":"3","tx_kumanokodo_gap":"40","tx_kumanokodo_heading":"","tx_kumanokodo_items":"0","tx_kumanokodo_items2":"0","tx_kumanokodo_label":"","tx_kumanokodo_layout":"stack","tx_kumanokodo_legend_boundary":"","tx_kumanokodo_legend_end":"","tx_kumanokodo_legend_walked":"","tx_kumanokodo_link":"","tx_kumanokodo_link2":"","tx_kumanokodo_link2_label":"","tx_kumanokodo_link_label":"","tx_kumanokodo_links":"0","tx_kumanokodo_meta":"","tx_kumanokodo_number":"","tx_kumanokodo_parent":"1486","tx_kumanokodo_path":"","tx_kumanokodo_rule":"1","tx_kumanokodo_space":"default","tx_kumanokodo_tone":"paper","tx_kumanokodo_variant":"default","tx_kumanokodo_vertical":"","uploads_description":"0","uploads_type":"0"}

中辺路では、家族経営の小さな宿、民宿に泊まる。夕食と朝食が付くことが多く、夕食は早い。

高原と近露には数軒しかない。春と秋は数か月前に満室になるので、全行程をまとめて予約するのがよい。

田辺市観光協会の予約サービスは英語で、ルート全体の宿を予約できる。

Takijiri is reached by bus from Kii-Tanabe station, which is on the JR line from Osaka. The ride takes about forty minutes.

Along the route, buses link the villages several times a day. They make it easy to shorten a day, and to get back to the coast from Hongu or Nachi.

Luggage can be sent ahead between the main villages. Book it through the Tanabe tourism office one day before.

Takijiri erreicht man mit dem Bus ab dem Bahnhof Kii-Tanabe, der an der JR-Strecke von Osaka liegt. Die Fahrt dauert etwa vierzig Minuten.

Entlang der Route verbinden Busse die Orte mehrmals am Tag. So lässt sich ein Tag verkürzen, und man kommt von Hongu oder Nachi zurück an die Küste.

Gepäck lässt sich zwischen den größeren Orten vorausschicken. Gebucht wird es einen Tag vorher über das Tourismusbüro in Tanabe.

滝尻へは、大阪からのJR線にある紀伊田辺駅からバスで行く。所要時間は約40分。

ルート沿いの集落は一日に何本かのバスで結ばれている。一日を短くしたり、本宮や那智から海沿いへ戻ったりするのに便利。

主な集落の間では荷物を先に送れる。前日までに田辺市観光協会で予約する。
The old imperial route from Tanabe to the three grand shrines of Kumano. We walked it in four days in April, from Takijiri to Nachi.

ウォークの終点。那智の滝の前に青岸渡寺の三重塔が立ち、その隣に熊野那智大社がある。

那智からは海沿いへバスが出ている。勝浦では港を渡る船で旅館へ向かう。
4日目 · 4月23日: 湯の峰 → 那智

One of the oldest hot springs in Japan, a short walk from Hongu. The bath houses stand along a stream in a narrow valley.

In late April carp streamers hung across the stream for Children’s Day. We sat in an outdoor bath under a wooden roof before dinner.

日本最古級の温泉のひとつで、本宮から少し歩いたところにある。狭い谷の沢沿いに湯屋が並ぶ。

4月の終わり、こどもの日を前に鯉のぼりが沢をまたいでいた。夕食の前に、木の屋根の下の露天風呂に浸かった。

The lantern gate at the edge of the village is hard to miss. The middle lantern shows the three-legged crow, the messenger of the Kumano deities.

{"CType":"text","assets":"0","bodytext":"

Der Morgen begann über den Wolken und endete an einem Tor aus Papierlaternen. Dazwischen Steinpflaster, das auch nass griffig bleibt, ein Bach unter den Zedern und eine leuchtend orange Krabbe, die für die Kamera stillhielt.

Um sieben Wolken im Tal. Steinpflaster, ein Bach, mittags eine Landkrabbe, um 17:28 das Laternentor von Chikatsuyu.

Früh genug losgehen, um Takahara bei Tageslicht zu erreichen; die erste Stunde ist steil, und dazwischen gibt es nichts.
Start early enough to reach Takahara in daylight; the first hour is steep and there is nothing in between.

At twenty to four we were at the river in Takijiri, a quarter of an hour later on the trail. The first hour does not pretend: steps, roots, then more steps.

On the trail at a quarter to four. 3.7 km, almost all of it uphill, to a village that sits above the valley.
